description: Solo developer and Computer Science student specializing in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. Experienced in Python, Java, full-stack web development, and AI-driven solutions. Working independently on The Earth Information Jukebox challenge to build an innovative, data-driven application.
summary: EarthSound turns NASA Earth Information Center images into live sound. A scan line moves across each image and its colours become drones, wind, notes and crackle, so blind and low-vision users can hear Earth data.
details:
EarthSound is a web "Earth Jukebox". It pairs NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations with sound that is generated live in the browser, so Earth science can be heard as well as seen.

How it works:

1. The user picks one of six NASA Earth images (or uploads their own).

2. A scan line moves from left to right across the image in 60 columns.

3. In each column, pixel colours are sorted into classes with a ruleset written for that image.

4. Each class has a sound: drone, wind, notes, soft notes, crackle or short blips.

5. Notes are snapped to a musical scale (pentatonic, major or minor) so the result is pleasant to listen to. For classes that use pitch, higher in the image means higher pitch.

The six images and their sounds:

- Forest height (GEDI): ocean = low drone, vegetation = notes, cloud = wind.

- Carbon dioxide (DYAMOND): haze = low drone, dense orange plumes = crackle, snow and cloud = wind.

- Night lights 2012 to 2023: purple (more light) = high chime, orange (less light) = low note, white (no change) = soft note.

- Sea surface currents and temperature: each colour range has its own pitch, blue lowest and red highest.

- Aerosols: purple = deep drone, green = wind, orange and red = crackle.

- Lightning from the ISS: each flash is a short blip.

Accessibility is a core goal: full keyboard control, a "Describe" button that reads the image description and the current column aloud (Web Speech API), a live text readout of what is under the scan line, a high-contrast mode, visible focus outlines, a skip link and ARIA labels.

Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, the Canvas API and the Web Audio API. It runs entirely in the browser with no server and no audio files. It is hosted on GitHub Pages and the code is open source (MIT license): https://github.com/Sachinpal-pal/Earthsound

Limitations: the colour-to-sound rules are an artistic mapping that follows the colours of each visualization, not a measurement of the data. Future work: more EIC datasets, a year-versus-year comparison by ear, and user-adjustable sound rules.

Team: SoloInnovator (solo participant: Sachin Pal).

SI disclosure: Claude (Anthropic) was used for coding, debugging and troubleshooting the HTML, CSS and JavaScript, for building the presentation deck, and for planning. The sounds are synthesized live by this code (Web Audio API); no audio files and no SI-generated images are used. All images are NASA stills. The participant chose the concept and images, tested the app and made all decisions.
